topics.title: Electrical projects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state safety rules for electrical projects.
The students should be able to identify basic electrical components.
Introduction:
We have learned about electrical circuits in previous classes. Today we will apply this knowledge by creating simple wiring boards.
Content:
A wiring board is a board used to practice electrical connections. Safety is the first rule when working with electricity. Always turn off power before touching wires. Common components include switches, bulbs, sockets, and wires. In Nigeria, we use 220V power. A simple project could be wiring a small bulb with a switch. Use proper tools like screwdrivers and pliers. Insulate all connections with electrical tape to prevent shock.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to create a simple circuit on a wooden board, connecting a bulb, switch, and power source using proper safety measures.
Evaluation questions:
What is the most important rule when working with electricity?
List three components used in electrical wiring.
Why should we insulate electrical connections?
Summary:
Electrical projects require strict safety measures and proper use of components to create functional circuits.

topics.title: Plumbing basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different types of pipes and fittings.
The students should be able to demonstrate how to join pipes properly.
Introduction:
We see plumbing systems in our homes and schools. Today we will learn about the basic components and how to join them together.
Content:
Pipes are tubes used to carry water or gas. Common types include PVC, copper, and galvanized pipes. Fittings connect pipes at corners, T-junctions, and ends. In Nigeria, PVC pipes are popular for water supply because they are affordable and durable. To join pipes, we use cement for PVC and solder for copper. Always measure and cut pipes straight for proper connections. Practice on scrap pieces before working on actual projects. Check joints for leaks after assembly.
Class activity:
Students will practice cutting and joining PVC pipes using cement, creating simple T-junctions and corner connections on scrap pieces.
Evaluation questions:
Name two types of pipes used in plumbing.
What is used to join PVC pipes together?
Why is it important to measure pipes accurately before cutting?
Summary:
Proper plumbing requires knowledge of pipe types and correct joining techniques to ensure leak-free connections.

topics.title: Geometric construction
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to construct different polygons using geometric tools.
The students should be able to draw perfect circles with a compass.
Introduction:
We use shapes in many everyday objects. Today we will learn how to draw precise geometric shapes using basic tools.
Content:
Geometric construction involves creating shapes using tools like compass, ruler, and protractor. A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides. Common polygons include triangles, squares, pentagons, and hexagons. To construct a regular polygon, divide 360 degrees by the number of sides. For example, a hexagon has six sides, so each angle is 60 degrees. Circles are drawn with a compass by setting the desired radius and rotating the tool. In Nigeria, market stalls often have circular designs that require precise construction. Always use sharp pencils and hold tools firmly for accuracy.
Class activity:
Students will construct a regular hexagon and a circle with a diameter of 10cm using geometric tools, then decorate their constructions.
Evaluation questions:
What tool is used to draw circles?
How many sides does a hexagon have?
What is the angle measure for each interior angle of a regular pentagon?
Summary:
Geometric construction requires precision and proper use of tools to create accurate shapes and forms.

topics.title: Sectioning
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the purpose of section views in technical drawings.
The students should be able to create simple section views of basic objects.
Introduction:
When we want to see inside an object, we can imagine cutting it. In technical drawing, we show this with section views.
Content:
Section views show the inside of an object as if it has been cut open. This helps us see internal features that would be hidden in regular views. The cutting plane is indicated with a line showing where the cut was made. In Nigeria, when building houses, engineers use section views to show wall structures. Different types of sectioning include full sections, half sections, and offset sections. When drawing sections, we use section lines (hatching) to show the cut surfaces. Common hatching patterns are at 45-degree angles with consistent spacing. Always label cutting planes and sections clearly.
Class activity:
Students will take a simple wooden block, draw its orthographic views, then create a section view showing the internal features.
Evaluation questions:
What is the purpose of a section view?
What are the lines called that show where an object has been cut?
Name two types of sectioning methods.
Summary:
Section views help us understand the internal structure of objects by showing them as if cut open along a specific plane.

topics.title: Fastening methods
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different types of fasteners and their uses.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper techniques for using nails, screws, and rivets.
Introduction:
We use different methods to join materials together. Today we will learn about various fastening techniques used in workshops.
Content:
Fasteners are used to join materials together. Common types include nails, screws, bolts, rivets, and welding. Nails are quick to use but may loosen over time. Screws provide stronger connections and can be removed. In Nigeria, carpenters often use both nails and screws depending on the project. Rivets are permanent fasteners used in metalwork, like in the construction of danfo buses. Welding joins metals by melting them together at high temperatures. When choosing fasteners, consider material strength, load requirements, and whether the joint needs to be permanent or removable. Always use the right size and type for your project.
Class activity:
Students will practice joining pieces of wood using nails and screws, and join metal pieces using pop rivets, comparing the strength of each method.
Evaluation questions:
Name three types of fasteners.
When might you choose screws over nails?
What is welding used for?
Summary:
Different fastening methods are suitable for different materials and project requirements, each with advantages and limitations.

topics.title: Woodwork: finishing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the importance of wood finishing.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper sanding and planing techniques.
Introduction:
After building a wooden object, the surface needs preparation before painting or varnishing. Today we will learn proper finishing techniques.
Content:
Wood finishing prepares the surface for treatment and improves appearance. Planing makes wood surfaces flat and smooth using a plane tool. Sanding uses sandpaper to remove rough spots and prepare the wood for finishing. In Nigeria, carpenters often use locally made planes and imported sandpaper. Always sand with the grain of the wood for best results. Start with coarse sandpaper (80-120 grit) and progress to finer grits (220-320) for smooth surfaces. Fill holes and cracks with wood filler before sanding. After sanding, wipe the wood with a clean cloth to remove dust before applying finish. Proper finishing protects wood from moisture and damage.
Class activity:
Students will practice planing and sanding pieces of scrap wood, progressing through different grits of sandpaper to achieve a smooth finish.
Evaluation questions:
Why is wood finishing important?
What is the proper sequence of sanding grits?
What should you do to wood surfaces after sanding but before applying finish?
Summary:
Proper wood finishing techniques prepare surfaces for treatment and improve both appearance and durability of wooden objects.

topics.title: Metalwork: forging basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify basic forging tools and equipment.
The students should be able to demonstrate simple bending techniques on metal.
Introduction:
Forging is shaping metal using heat and force. We will learn basic forging techniques used to create simple metal objects.
Content:
Forging is the process of shaping metal through the application of force, often using heat. Basic tools include an anvil, hammer, tongs, and forge. In Nigeria, traditional blacksmiths use charcoal forges and simple hammers. Always wear protective gear when forging, including heat-resistant gloves and safety glasses. Heating metal makes it softer and easier to shape. Common forging techniques include bending, drawing out (making longer), and upsetting (making thicker). For simple bends, heat the metal until it is cherry red, then place it on the anvil and bend with hammer strikes. Practice on scrap metal before working on projects. Always quench hot metal in water to cool it properly.
Class activity:
Students will practice bending heated metal rods into simple shapes using forging hammers and anvils, following proper safety procedures.
Evaluation questions:
What protective equipment should be worn when forging?
What color should metal be before forging?
Name two basic forging techniques.
Summary:
Forging requires proper safety measures and technique to shape metal effectively using heat and force.

topics.title: Design process
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the steps in the design process.
The students should be able to apply the design process to solve a simple problem.
Introduction:
Before building anything, we need a plan. Today we will learn the systematic process used to design solutions to problems.
Content:
The design process is a systematic approach to creating solutions. It begins with identifying a need or problem. For example, in Nigeria, many communities need better ways to carry water from wells. The next step is research to understand the problem better. Then brainstorm possible solutions without judgment. Select the best idea and develop it through sketches and models. Create a prototype (test model) and evaluate its performance. Based on feedback, improve the design before final production. Throughout the process, document ideas and decisions. This systematic approach ensures that the final product meets the original need effectively.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to identify a problem in the school, then apply the design process to develop a solution, creating sketches and a simple prototype.
Evaluation questions:
What is the first step in the design process?
Why is prototyping important?
What should you do after evaluating a prototype?
Summary:
The design process provides a structured approach to creating solutions that effectively address identified needs and problems.

topics.title: Project build
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to follow a plan to construct a simple project.
The students should be able to document the steps taken during construction.
Introduction:
Now that we have designed our projects, we will learn how to build them systematically while recording our progress.
Content:
Building a project requires careful planning and execution. Start by gathering all materials and tools needed. Review your design plans and create a step-by-step construction sequence. In Nigeria, local craftspeople often work with limited resources but still produce quality work. Measure and mark all components carefully before cutting or shaping. Assemble pieces according to your plan, checking for accuracy at each step. Document your progress by taking photos or sketches at key stages. Note any challenges encountered and how you solved them. Test your project as you build to ensure each part works correctly. Quality control ensures the final product meets your design specifications.
Class activity:
Students will build a small wooden storage box following their own designs, documenting the construction process with notes and sketches.
Evaluation questions:
Why is it important to gather all materials before starting construction?
What should you document during project building?
How can testing during construction help improve the final product?
Summary:
Successful project building requires careful planning, systematic execution, and proper documentation of the construction process.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer questions from previous topics covered this term.
The students should be able to solve BECE-style questions on Basic Technology.
Introduction:
As we approach the end of term, we will revise key topics and practice questions similar to those in the BECE examination.
Content:
Revision involves going over important concepts from this term. Key topics include electrical projects, plumbing basics, geometric construction, sectioning, fastening methods, wood finishing, metalwork forging, and the design process. Practice questions help prepare for the Basic Technology BECE exam. Questions may include multiple choice, theory, and practical problem-solving. When answering theory questions, be concise and specific. For practical questions, show all steps in your solution. Time management is important during exams. Practice with past questions to understand the exam format and question types. Focus on areas where you need improvement during revision sessions.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to solve past BECE questions on Basic Technology, then present their solutions to the class for discussion.
Evaluation questions:
Name three topics covered this term in Basic Technology.
What should you focus on when revising for an exam?
How can practicing past questions help with exam preparation?
Summary:
Regular revision and practice with exam-style questions are essential for success in the BECE examination.
